two lessening points of light] The tips of the setting moon’s crescent, of which the middle is already
in darkness (‘the divided frame’). The two points of light replace the eyes of the dream-maid (lines 179,
489–92) that have hitherto obsessed him.
 stagnate] An earlier form of stagnant.
 Even as a vapour . . . Eclipses it] ‘like a sunlit cloud in attendance on the sun until it sets’.
 ‘It is quite in Shelley’s manner . . . to go back to and bring together his illustrations. Here the poet’s
frame is a lute, a bright stream, a dream of youth. The lute is still, the stream is dark and dry, the dream is
unremembered’ (Stopford Brooke, Poems of Shelley (1880) 324). The illustrations themselves recall lines
41–9 (poet as wind-harp), 149–51 (dream of youth), and 494–514 (stream of life).
